Hub/Care journey/Box and unboxing
Care journey

Box and unboxing.

What arrives at the door, what is inside, and ideas for the moment he opens it. Plain on the outside, warm on the inside. Nothing here ships until operations, the pharmacy and legal have checked it.

DiscretionIn the boxPrinted piecesMicrocopyPrint specsIdeasSustainabilityOpen items
Current · U-29

The outside, the cards and the start ideas are decided (U-29); supplier, carrier and pharmacy checks stay with operations (R-68). Square brackets mark values that operations, the pharmacy, the clinical team or legal fill in. Mockups are flat drawings for review, not print files.

Current · U-29

Outside: the mailer carries one short, discreet line that never says what is inside: "Packed with care, just for you.", with a small outline capsule before it. Sender name on the shipping label: unifiedmeds. Welcome card greeting: "Welcome to unifiedmeds." Cards: 4 × 6 in. Ideas: start with the three easy ones. Leaflet: no sleeve or wrap for the pharmacy leaflet at launch.

Discreet from the doorstep.

A neighbour, a partner or a mail room sees the mailer. The member sees what is inside. The brand starts once the box is open.

Quiet outside.

No category, no medicine, no symptom and no "men's health" on the mailer, the tape or the label. Nothing shows through. One short line is printed with a small outline capsule (decided); neither names or hints at what is inside.

The brand starts inside.

The inner box carries the seal and the capsule. The welcome card is the first thing he reads.

Current · U-29Sender name: unifiedmeds.

The shipping label says unifiedmeds as the sender, with the return address from operations. The word "meds" sits inside the name, so nothing else on the outside adds to it: no logo, no product, no category.

No windows, no product shapes.

No see-through panels, no bottle-shaped boxes, no tape or sticker that hints at what is inside.

Outside of the mailerA neighbour seesThe member getsStatus
A · PlainA kraft box and a label from unifiedmedsFull privacy; the brand waits insideThe base
A + one lineA kraft box, one short line that says nothing about the content, and the labelA small warm moment at the door, still privateCurrent · U-29
B · Capsule markA kraft box with an abstract outlineA box he recognises at the doorTo confirm
C · Seal on the lidThe name unifiedmeds, which includes "meds"Brand presence at the doorNot recommended

Decided (U-29): one short printed line outside and unifiedmeds as the sender name. Whether the capsule mark (B) joins the line stays open, once operations confirm what the carrier and the pharmacy require.

What is in the box.

From the outside in, in the order he meets each piece. The pharmacy fills and labels the bottle; the brand frames it and never touches what the pharmacy supplies.

  1. 1MailerOperations

    Kraft, sized to the inner box so nothing moves. One short printed line with a small outline capsule. Shipping label with unifiedmeds as the sender.

  2. 2Inner box lidBrand

    Deep Teal, the reversed seal, one capsule cropped by the edge. The first branded moment.

  3. 3Welcome cardBrand

    4 × 6 in, two sides. The greeting, "Welcome to unifiedmeds.", and three things to know before he starts.

  4. 4Next-steps cardBrand and clinical team

    6 × 4 in landscape. His account, the check-in and how refills work.

  5. 5Bottle in a card insertPharmacy

    The bottle as dispensed, with its pharmacy label untouched. The insert holds one or two bottles upright.

  6. 6Sample, optionalLegal first

    A non-prescription companion product, only after legal review. Never a prescription product.

  7. 7Patient information leafletPharmacy

    Printed and supplied by the pharmacy, placed as supplied. No sleeve or wrap at launch (decided); the content is never edited.

  8. 8Inner box trayBrand and supplier

    Deep Teal outside, Paper inside. Holds everything in place with no plastic fill.

Two labels on one bottle.

The brand label (Packaging, R-89) and the pharmacy's dispensing label, with the member's name and directions, must live together. Where each goes is an open item with the pharmacy.

"Patient" stays in one place.

The glossary says member, not patient (R-57). The leaflet keeps its own name because the pharmacy issues it. Our cards say "the leaflet from your pharmacy".

The printed pieces.

Paper ground, Deep Teal text, DM Serif headlines at 24 or more, the seal in Navy. Copy is short and warm and makes no promise about results or timing (R-58, R-68).

PieceLineWhy it is safe
Welcome card"Welcome to unifiedmeds."Warm and plain; names the brand, not the treatment
Welcome card"Everything you need to begin is in this box."Describes the box, promises nothing about the treatment
Welcome card"Follow your label. Take it as your provider prescribed it."Points to the pharmacy label; gives no dose
Welcome card"[Safety line from the clinical team]"Clinical wording is never written by the brand
Next-steps card"Your provider reviews your plan before each refill."Names the licensed provider as responsible (R-64); no timing (R-68)
Leaflet sleeve (not at launch)"From your pharmacy."Frames the leaflet without speaking for it

Microcopy, decided.

Avi chose option 1 in both lists (U-29); the other options stay on file. Each line is short, warm and plain, makes no claim and names no product. The outside lines also say nothing about health, medicine or the category, so a neighbour learns nothing from them.

Outside of the mailer.

Current · U-29 · option 1
  1. Packed with care, just for you.Chosen. Warm and personal; printed with a small outline capsule before it.
  2. Delivered quietly. Open when you like.Says discretion without saying why.
  3. Handled with care, from our door to yours.About the journey, not the content.
  4. Here when you're ready.The shortest; calm and patient.

Every line is one colour, 18 to 24 pt, away from the label, and never next to a word that hints at health.

Welcome card greeting.

Current · U-29 · option 1
  1. Welcome to unifiedmeds.Chosen. The plain welcome; shown on the card above.
  2. Glad you're here.Short and warm; the brand is already on the lid.
  3. Good to have you with us.Says he is a member, not a customer.
  4. Your box, your pace.Matches the discretion of the outside.
  5. Hello, and thank you.Simple thanks, nothing promised.

The greeting sits in DM Serif at 44 on the 4 × 6 card, on one or two lines. The two lines below it stay as they are.

Ideas for the unboxing.

Twelve ideas, grouped. Effort is a first guess for design, sourcing and approval together.

Current · U-29

Start with the three easy ideas: brand inside, plain outside; a note from the care team; the account in his pocket (the wallet card). The other nine wait.

The box itself.

Brand inside, plain outside.

The inner box carries the seal and the capsule; the mailer stays quiet.

Start here · decidedEffort · Medium
A box worth keeping.

A lift-off lid sized for a drawer, so the bottle has a home after the first day.

Effort · MediumStorage advice comes from the pharmacy leaflet; the box never contradicts it.
One line under the flap.

A single printed line inside the mailer, seen only once it is open: "[Line to be written]".

Effort · LowInside only. Nothing shows while the box is closed.

Paper extras.

A note from the care team.

A short printed note, signed "The unifiedmeds care team".

Start here · decidedEffort · LowNever signed with a provider's name unless that provider wrote it.
The account in his pocket.

A wallet card: how to message the provider, track an order and plan a refill.

Start here · decidedEffort · LowNo health details on it, so it is fine if someone else finds it.
Questions for my provider.

A slim notebook for the questions he wants to ask at the next check-in.

Effort · MediumPlain cover with no category on it.

Complementary products.

A non-prescription sample.

A small sample of a companion product that fits the category.

Effort · HighLegal review required. Over-the-counter only, never free medicine, and nothing implies it works with the treatment.
A travel case for the bottle.

A small zip case that holds the original bottle, label and all.

Effort · MediumThe medicine stays in the pharmacy bottle; the case never replaces it.

Merchandise.

A capsule pouch.

A canvas pouch with the capsule outline only, no name.

Effort · MediumThings he carries in public follow the same discretion choice as the mailer.
A capsule keyring.

The capsule outline in metal, small enough for any key set.

Effort · HighNeeds tooling and a minimum order; a later phase.

Coupons and referral.

Refer a friend.

A card with a personal code he can pass on, if he chooses to.

Effort · MediumLegal review required. Referral rewards around prescription products are regulated. The reward is never free or discounted medicine and never depends on a prescription.
A thank-you credit.

A one-time credit toward the consultation fee or a non-prescription product.

Effort · LowLegal review required. A dollar amount, never a blanket percentage (R-61).

Made to be recycled.

Every piece is paper, so the whole box goes in one bin. The bottle follows the pharmacy's advice.

Paper all the way.

Kraft mailer, paperboard box, card or pulp insert. One material family.

Right-sized.

The inner box fits the bottles and the mailer fits the inner box, so nothing needs filling.

Uncoated and water-based.

No foil, no laminate, no plastic window, so the print does not stop the recycling.

No plastic fill.

No air pillows, foam or shrink wrap. If something needs padding, it is paper.

No claim we cannot prove.

Say "recyclable" only where the supplier certifies it, with a plain instruction on the inner box.

The bottle follows the pharmacy.

How to dispose of the bottle and any unused medicine comes from the leaflet, never from the brand.
